comment: WORST PROFESSOR EVER. He honestly does not care about what grades his students get and when you go to office hours he is rude and useless. I do not understand why this man is still teaching he clearly is over it and thinks class is a time for jokes and fun. I did not learn ANYTHING in class. What a waste of my time!!!! I am disappointed.

Dr. Allison is my favorite professor at the University of Richmond; so much so that I've made sure to take a class with him all 4 of my years year. He is such a caring, inspiring, and intelligent man who cares so much about what he teachers, but cares even more about his students! I can't put into words how amazing he is! Everyone deserves a Dr. A!

Dr. Allison is the sweetest man alive. He is really passionate about what he teaches. He really cares about his students and wants what's best for them. I have taken many classes with him and they are all easy A's. However, if you want more of a challenge, his classes can be really boring and not as rewarding as it's a lot of review of intro stuff

Worst professor ever. Does not give specific guidelines and it seems like he just doesn't care about anyones grades. Didn't learn anything in class and the exams were heavily based on the textbook, which we NEVER covered in class.

I loved this FYS! Would highly recommend, especially if you're interested in psychology. Homework consisted of reading 10-15 page articles, which were all interesting. Some classes he presented and reviewed while others students presented on. The whole class leads up to a 15 page paper that will be published as a chapter in a book.
Makes the course fun! There is not alway powerpoints, so make sure to write down notes.

He's super enthusiastic and interesting, but his midterm was soooo hard which lowered a lot of people's grades. His papers are also really long, but creative so if you like creative writing then you should be ok. Every class is a student-pair led discussion which gets annoying because the discussions from those are never that great.

Hard midterm and final, not normal for a FYS to have one let alone both. 3-4 500 word essays, daily readings, 2 more essays, 2 presentations and this past semester he decided to assign a 25 page paper. All the readings are from his own handbook. The only reason I got an A is because he rounds to whole grades and I just barely got a 90.

Take his Heroes and Villains FYS. It's a lot of reading, but so is every other FYS. At least this one is fun and interesting. Participation matters a lot. Read the assigned readings, participate in class discussions (it's almost entirely a discussion based class), and you're guaranteed a good grade.

SO enthusiastic which is great. Makes concepts easy and interesting. Test is 50% from the textbook (never taught in class) so STUDY EARLY. The class portion is easy as long as you took good notes in class. His class seems like a breeze, but you can get caught if you don't prepare for his test. Good man who is ready to help!

Professor Allison's love for Psychology was refreshing. Note taking was extremely easy b/c he's very clear and don't rush. He was the only teacher this year that tested us on textbook material, which was overwhelming. Other than that, the section of the test that was on in-class material was pretty easy (just take good notes and study them).

Allison is a space cadet. The man is very passionate about his subject, but the information he teaches you has nothing to do with the information on the tests. Really fun class though, learn some interesting topics in creative ways.

He expects you to read the book and his test was based mainly on the book rather than what he explained in class. He does a lot of hands-on activities during class that really help major concepts stick. He is not too hard of a grader.
He is super nice, his tests are challenging but the class is interesting
He's an easy going teacher. Lots of reading. Didn't really get the time to read the readings. He's not super easy but he's not extremely difficult. He's an ok teacher.
Dr. Allison is the best. Will always stand out as one of my favorite professors at UR. Helpful, approachable, caring. Definitely take him. His classes are fun.

Dr. Allison is an amazing professor and a very interesting person. Core is no longer a class however he is teaching a seminar  called Heroes and Villains based on a book he collaborated on. I would definitely recommend him to any freshman! If you can't get his seminar try taking one of his ball room dancing classes over the year. Very fun!
Dr. Allison is absolutely awesome. Even though Core is done, freshman should definitely take his freshman seminar. He is funny, really nice, charming, handsome, and just absolutely incredible.

So geeky, still acts like a college student (from the 80's)...class is interesting, he makes it fun. Great professor. Not a demanding class, few papers, not a hard grader.  Gets everyone involved. Take good notes for the test... Doesn't really follow book, so no one reads the book, but the information is definitely on the tests.

Exams are easy if you take thorough notes,exams are open note. 2nd exam includes a section from a huge book we never used, he said to read on own, but he went over it.3 papers arent demanding, last is group project(paper option group or individual). Sometimes he's unclear w/ SPSS functions. Kinda demanding w/ 313 class and lab 1st 1/2 of semester.
Wonderful professor!!! Very informative and approachable.  I felt like he wanted me to succeed.  He drew me into the class with his humor and his own enthusiasm for the subject.
Coolest prof I had at UR! Upperclassmen should take his social cognition class.
one terrific professor...intelligent, humorous...just a great person....best class i ever had
could have engaged us more...
amazing professor. Had a good sense of humor...made the material interesting.
